name: SPF No.2 lumber
description: Spruce-pine-fir, grade No.2: the everyday framing lumber at US big-box stores. Reference design values, unadjusted; size and other adjustment factors are applied by the solver.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4A (visually graded dimension lumber, 2"–4" thick, 2" & wider), Spruce-Pine-Fir No.1/No.2 row (NLGA): Fb 875, Ft 450, Fv 135, Fc⊥ 425, Fc 1150, E 1,400,000 psi; G 0.42; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Douglas fir-larch No.2 lumber
description: Douglas fir-larch, grade No.2: stiffer and stronger than SPF; the common framing lumber in the West. Reference design values, unadjusted.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4A (visually graded dimension lumber, 2"–4" thick, 2" & wider), Douglas Fir-Larch No.2 row: Fb 900, Ft 575, Fv 180, Fc⊥ 625, Fc 1350, E 1,600,000 psi; G 0.50; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Southern yellow pine No.2 lumber
description: Southern pine, grade No.2: dense, strong framing lumber common in the South and East. Southern pine values are size-specific; these are the 2x8 row. Reference values, unadjusted.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4B (Southern Pine, size-specific), No.2, 8" wide row: Fb 925, Ft 550, Fv 175, Fc⊥ 565, Fc 1350, E 1,400,000 psi (the 2"–4" wide row is higher: Fb 1100, Ft 675, Fc 1450); G 0.55; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Pressure-treated lumber No.2 (above ground)
description: Pressure-treated No.2 lumber for above-ground use (UC3B), such as sill plates on concrete. The species varies by region (southern pine in the East, hem-fir or Douglas fir in the West); design values here are SPF No.2 as the conservative case.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4A (visually graded dimension lumber, 2"–4" thick, 2" & wider), Spruce-Pine-Fir No.1/No.2 row (NLGA): Fb 875, Ft 450, Fv 135, Fc⊥ 425, Fc 1150, E 1,400,000 psi; G 0.42; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Pressure-treated southern pine No.2 (ground contact)
description: Pressure-treated southern pine No.2 rated for ground contact (UC4A): posts set in soil or concrete, and framing near the ground. Reference values (2x8 row), unadjusted; wet-service factors apply.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4B (Southern Pine, size-specific), No.2, 8" wide row: Fb 925, Ft 550, Fv 175, Fc⊥ 565, Fc 1350, E 1,400,000 psi (the 2"–4" wide row is higher: Fb 1100, Ft 675, Fc 1450); G 0.55; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Western red cedar lumber
description: Western red cedar (graded as Western Cedars No.2): naturally decay-resistant and light, for trim, siding, fences and exposed posts. Weaker than framing lumber. Reference values, unadjusted.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4A (visually graded dimension lumber, 2"–4" thick, 2" & wider), Western Cedars No.2 row: Fb 700, Ft 425, Fv 155, Fc⊥ 425, Fc 650, E 1,000,000 psi; G 0.36; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Redwood lumber (construction heart/common)
description: Redwood, Construction grade (sold as construction heart or construction common): decay-resistant heartwood for decks, fences and trim. Construction grade is tabulated for 2–4in widths only; reference values, unadjusted.
source: NDS 2018 Supplement Table 4A (visually graded dimension lumber, 2"–4" thick, 2" & wider), Redwood Construction row (2"–4" wide): Fb 825, Ft 475, Fv 160, Fc⊥ 425, Fc 925, E 900,000 psi; G 0.37; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A
